chunks: The Shaykh, critical Imam, core of the religion, beauty of the Imams, rarity of the age, Abu al-Qasim Ahmad b. Hamza al-Nu'aymi (may Allah lengthen his life) informed us. The Shaykh, Imam, scholar, ascetic, supporter of the religion, pillar of Islam, Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Muhammad b. Abi al-Hasan b. Abd al-Samad al-Tamimi (may Allah be pleased with him) informed us. The Shaykh, jurist, scholar, ornament of the religion, my father, informed us. The Shaykh, jurist, scholar, father Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Abd al-Samad b. Muhammad al-Tamimi informed us. The majestic master, the scholar, Abu al-Barakat Ali b. al-Husayn al-Alawi al-Juri (may Allah illuminate his grave) and the Shaykh Abu Bakr Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) informed us. They both said: The Shaykh, jurist, Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us on Friday, twelve nights remaining in Rajab, year 367. He said: The Shaykh Yahya b. Zayd b. al-Abbas b. al-Walid al-Bazzaz narrated to us in Kufa. He said: My uncle Ali b. al-Abbas narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Bishr b. Khalid al-Abdi narrated to us. He said: Amr b. Khalid narrated to us. He said: Abu Hamza al-Thumali narrated to us from Ali b. al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said:
A good saying increases one's wealth, boosts one's sustenance, prolongs one's lifespan, makes one beloved to one's family, and enters one into Paradise.

key_terms.القول الحسن: Good saying; virtuous, kind speech that brings blessings
key_terms.يثري المال: Increases wealth; enriches one's material possessions
key_terms.ينسئ في الاجل: Prolongs the lifespan; delays the appointed time of death

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of good speech according to Imam Zayn al-Abidin?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (as), the fourth Shia Imam, teaches that good speech brings five blessings: it increases wealth, boosts sustenance, prolongs life, endears one to family, and leads to Paradise. This hadith was narrated through a long chain of transmission going back to Shaykh al-Saduq's assembly in Kufa in 367 AH, emphasizing the comprehensive benefits of kind and virtuous speech in both worldly and spiritual dimensions.
